newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cie Bancaire to buy out units Cardif, UFB.
newsitem.headline: Cie Bancaire to buy out units Cardif, UFB.

text.p: French specialist retail financial services company Cie Bancaire announced on Wednesday that it offers to buy out its two units, Cardif and UFB Locabail, for a maximum total investment of three billion francs.

Cie Bancaire, majority-owned by French financial group Paribas, said in a statement it was offering 900 francs per share for the 39.4 percent of Cardif and 600 francs per share for the 27.5 percent of UFB Locabail held by the public.
It said it planned a maximum two billion franc capital increase to finance the bids of which it said Paribas may subscribe 50 percent.
Cie Bancaire said its bid for Cardif would be followed by a merger between Cardif and itself.
It said the operation was "aimed at increasing is profitability and giving more flexibility to its financial management in attractive conditions for the shareholders involved."
Shares of Cardif closed at 655 francs on Tuesday while shares of UFB Locabail closed at 522 francs.
It said the capital increase to finance the transactions was planned to be carried out before the end of the year.

"Cie Bancaire plans to proceed before the end of the year with a maximum two billion franc cash capital increase with preferential subscription rights," it said. "In this case, Cie Financiere de Paribas will subscribe to the level of its holding, 50 percent."
UFB Locabail recorded a 1996 net attributable profit of 225 million francs while Cardif's profit totalled 340.1 million francs.
